slides.name: Pond water
slides.description: Six distinct photographic cutouts, each placed once. Three different photographed ciliates move on computed paths. The source cultures and freshwater mat are assembled, not a natural abundance sample.

objects.note: A paramecium: one cell that swims. The green dots are algae living inside it.
A rotifer: a tiny animal. Its crown of hairs moves water toward its mouth.
A diatom: one cell inside a patterned shell. The long lines belong to that shell.
A thread from a freshwater microbial mat. Long strands cross this sample.
A paramecium: one cell that swims. This photographed cell has no green algae inside.
A paramecium: one cell that swims. The long body has a different shape from the green one.

slides.trayDescription: Wet mount. Scan with the stage knobs.

slides.name: Onion skin
slides.description: Unstained skin with the source LED cast corrected by per-channel white balance, and separate Lugol-iodine fields from a monochrome camera. These are different cells, not a before-and-after record.

objects.note: Onion skin without stain. Long cell walls mark the edges of neighbouring cells.

iodine.note: Onion skin stained with iodine. This photograph was taken with a monochrome camera.
Onion skin stained with iodine. Dark round structures inside the walls are nuclei.

slides.trayDescription: Compare unstained and iodine photographs with Prepare mount.

slides.name: Human hair
slides.description: Human hair over a ruled counting chamber. The known grid provides the physical scale.

objects.note: A human hair on a counting grid. The small squares are about 50 micrometres wide.

slides.trayDescription: Hair on a counting grid. Turn focus along its length.

slides.name: Bahamas sand
slides.description: Real shell-rich sand from French Bay, San Salvador. Original reflected-light photograph.

objects.note: Sand from a beach in the Bahamas. Some grains are pieces of shells.

slides.trayDescription: Beach sand photographed in reflected light.

slides.name: Hosta leaf
slides.description: Two finite epidermis fields from a water-mounted Hosta leaf, at different source samplings.

objects.note: A leaf surface. Look for the boundaries between its cells.
A closer view of a leaf surface. Look for the boundaries between its cells.

slides.name: Crane-fly wing
slides.description: A photographed crane-fly wing. The 2 mm source bar measures 206 pixels; the cropped tile is 13.79 mm wide, including background. It is not a measured wing length. Fine hairs are not resolved in this source.

objects.note: A crane-fly wing. The dark veins support its thin membrane.

slides.trayDescription: A crane-fly wing. Follow its veins with the stage knobs.

slides.name: Onion root tip
slides.description: A real acetocarmine root-tip field from CIL:43552, with four separate Feulgen control close-ups inset at their physical sizes. They are different specimens and stains. Base-field scale is inferred, not calibrated; the insets retain measured 10 micrometre source bars.

objects.note: An onion root tip. Many cells have a round nucleus; a few have visible chromosomes.
Prophase: chromosomes become thick and visible inside a root-tip cell.
Metaphase in a squashed root-tip cell. The chromosomes are spread apart in this preparation.
Anaphase: two groups of chromosomes separate inside a dividing cell.
Telophase: two new nuclei form as a root-tip cell divides.

slides.trayDescription: A root-tip field with separate control close-ups.

slides.name: Blood smear
slides.description: Eight separately photographed Giemsa fields spread across the glass. Figure letters, gutters and scale bars are removed. Original sample context is on this slide’s Manual source page.

objects.note: A blood smear: pale discs are red blood cells. Some cells in this published sample contain malaria parasites.
A blood smear: pale discs are red blood cells. Some cells in this published sample contain malaria parasites.

slides.name: Cheek swab
slides.description: A real methylene-blue cheek field with dark nuclei. Pale source glass is alpha-masked using blue minus red; retained RGB pixels are unchanged. Scale is inferred from a typical cell edge, not measured on this camera. Cell size varies; this approximate field is for observation, not precision measurement.

objects.note: Cheek cells: flat cells from inside the mouth. A dark oval inside a cell is its nucleus.

slides.trayDescription: A methylene-blue cheek smear. Scale is approximate.

slides.name: Pond colony
slides.description: A fixed pond colony, photographed at nine focus positions, 25 micrometres apart. Turn focus through the field to see different depths.
slides.trayDescription: Fixed pond colony. Turn focus through nine photographs.

slides.name: Stage micrometer
slides.description: Exact code-drawn 1 mm stage micrometer: 100 divisions of 10 µm.
slides.trayDescription: An etched scale with ten-micrometre divisions.

paramecium.title: Characterization of Crystals in Ciliate Paramecium bursaria, Fig. 1a, three transmitted-light panels
paramecium.credit: Yuuki Kodama, Ayasa Kitatani, Yuriko Morita
paramecium.scale: First two panels: shared 20 micrometre bar measures about 69 pixels. Right panel: its separate 20 micrometre bar is 37 pixels end-to-end on row 362 of the original download. These are three distinct cultured individuals, not one natural pond sample.
paramecium.magnification: source optical microscopy; reproduced scale bar determines pixel size

rotifer.title: Adineta beysunae (10.3897-zookeys.941.50465) Figure 3.jpg
rotifer.credit: Zeng Y, Wei N, Wang Q, Iakovenko NS, Li Y, Yang Y (2020)
rotifer.scale: Photographic panel B only. Vertical 50 µm bar = approximately 538 original pixels. Drawing A excluded.

diatom.title: Bancsó 2021 Fig 7-8 Pinnularia viridis.jpg
diatom.scale: 20 µm bar = approximately 165 pixels in the downloaded 1280 px thumbnail. Scale measured after thumbnail resampling.

mat.title: 41396 2020 676 Fig4b.jpg
mat.credit: H. S. Tee, D. Waite, L. Payne, M. Middleditch, S. Wood, K. M. Handley
mat.scale: Lower-right panel: 20 µm bar = approximately 89 pixels. One unlabelled filament crop.

hair.title: Hemocytometer grid with human hair 100x.jpg
hair.scale: Known-size object: central haemocytometer fine squares, 50 µm, approximately 50 px. Inferred standard Neubauer grid pitch, not a camera calibration. Both axes agree within about 2%.

sand.title: Marine biogenous aragonite sand (modern; sandy beach at French Bay, San Salvador Island, Bahamas) (48739969587).jpg
sand.credit: Sara Beth Kopczynski, shared by James St. John
sand.scale: 2 mm white bar = approximately 280 pixels. Reflected-light source; not transmitted-light sand.

wing.title: Tipula dechangensis (10.3897-zookeys.1040.64376) Figures 1, 2.jpg
wing.credit: Men Q-L, Starkevich P, Saldaitis A (2021)
wing.scale: Full available source (1512 x 1314 px): 2.0 mm bar measures 206 px, or 9.71 um/px. The 1420 px crop is 13.79 mm wide including background; this is not an anatomical wing length. Article reports 14.3-16.8 mm wing length for the species. Source resolution limits high-power use.

onion-clear.title: Mobile-phone-based Rheinberg microscope with an LED array, Fig. 9a
onion-clear.credit: Yuma Ogasawara, Ryo Sugimoto, Ryoji Maruyama, Hidenobu Arimoto, Yosuke Tamada, Wataru Watanabe
onion-clear.scale: 100 µm bar = approximately 47 pixels. Brightfield panel a only.
onion-clear.magnification: source optical microscopy; reproduced scale bar determines pixel size

lens.title: Low-cost 3D-printed lenses for brightfield and fluorescence microscopy, Figs. 5C, 5E, 6D and 6F
lens.credit: Jay Christopher, Liam M Rooney, Mark Donnachie, Deepak Uttamchandani, Gail McConnell, Ralf Bauer
lens.scale: Fig. 5: 250 µm bar ≈64 px; Fig. 6: 50 µm bar ≈76 px. Unlabelled crops strictly within commercial-lens lower-left halves. Onion uses Lugol iodine; Hosta epidermis is a water mount.
lens.magnification: source optical microscopy; reproduced scale bar determines pixel size

cheek.title: Human epithelial cells stained with methylene blue dye
cheek.scale: Approximate only: 0.22 um per original pixel, using a roughly 250-pixel cell edge and a 55 um reference size. Prasad et al. control cells average 54.97 um; Romeo et al. independently describe mature buccal cells as 50-60 um on edge. These are variable biological sizes, not a camera calibration. Do not use this slide for precision measurement; use the source-bar-scaled blood fields instead.
cheek.magnification: Not stated by photographer; never used to invent a calibrated pixel size.

root.title: Exogenous application of mycotoxin fusaric acid, Fig. 4, control root-tip mitosis
root.scale: 10 µm bar = approximately 35 pixels. Four control fields; Feulgen staining, original photographic panels a–d.
root.magnification: source optical microscopy; reproduced scale bar determines pixel size

blood.title: Human Plasmodium knowlesi Infection, Fig. 1
blood.credit: J. J. van Hellemond and coauthors; CDC Emerging Infectious Diseases (2009)
blood.scale: Caption: 5 µm bar, approximately 28 pixels in this 600 px figure. Eight Giemsa-stained blood fields with malaria parasites. The uninfected cell near source x105,y50 spans about 42 pixels, independently approximately 7.5 µm.
blood.magnification: source blood-smear optical micrograph, magnification not stated

stack.title: High-contrast multifocus microscopy with a single camera and z-splitter prism, Supplement 1, Fig. S9b
stack.credit: Sheng Xiao, Howard Gritton, Hua-an Tseng, Dana Zemel, Xue Han, Jerome Mertz (2020)
stack.scale: 100 µm bar = approximately 98 pixels in extracted PDF JPEG. Nine simultaneous focal planes spaced 25 µm, +100 to -100 µm. Fixed Volvox in Eukitt; darkfield, original ImageJ green-fire-blue lookup table retained. Same registered crop for every plane.
stack.magnification: source 20×/0.5 NA objective; source darkfield, not a fluorescence simulation

meristem.title: CIL:43552, Allium cepa, root tip
meristem.scale: Approximate 0.22 um per pixel: nuclei around 80-110 pixels compared with roughly 18-24 um nuclei in the independently scaled Cavusoglu control fields. Archive supplies no pixel calibration. This is a size-based inference, unsuitable for precision measurement.
meristem.magnification: 40x / 0.65 NA stated by archive; not used to calculate pixel size
